retrieval_command: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/SysBioChalmers/yeast-GEM.git; cp data/testResults/essentialGenes.tsv data/testResults/README.md data/essentialGenes/README.md .

essentialGenes.tsv.note: one row per gene of the 1,107 benchmark genes with the repository's own TP/TN/FP/FN label, where TP is 'true non-essential' (model and experiment viable) and TN 'true essential' (both inviable); counts TP 933, FP 94, TN 65, FN 15

README.md.note: data/testResults/README.md; 'Latest release results' for 9.1.1: gene essentiality accuracy 0.9015356820234869, Python 3.12.14, cobrapy 0.32.1; caveat quoted: 'Note that the deletion collection was screened on complex medium supplemented for genetic markers, so it is not ideal ground truth; it is most useful for comparing model versions against each other.'

essentialGenes_data_README.md.note: data/essentialGenes/README.md: inviable_orfs.txt, 1191 entries (1122 unique), 'Essential ORFs from the Stanford yeast deletion project (14 aug 2011 snapshot)', source http://www-sequence.stanford.edu/group/yeast_deletion_project/downloads.html; verified_orfs.txt, 5061 unique ORFs, 'The verified set from SGD (27 August 2013)'

method: code/python/yeastgem/model_tests/essential_genes.py (and code/modelTests/essentialGenes.m): complete_Y7() sets the Kennedy synthetic complete medium (all exchanges closed, 28 constrained uptakes at -0.5, glucose r_1714 at -20, 15 unconstrained uptakes at -1000), cobra single_gene_deletion, growth ratio against the wild type, a gene is inviable when the ratio is below _KO_TOL = 1e-6; the 1,107 genes are the verified ORFs in the model; methodology 'Adapted from: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004530' (Heavner and Price 2015)
